veto_criteria_list.description: Offline capability failure (<2.0). System must function in remote areas without constant connectivity.
Input supply chain dependency failure (<2.0). Critical dependence on unavailable inputs (seeds, fertilizer).
Teacher/Facilitator training failure (<2.5). Solution unusable without adequately trained human facilitators.
Certification validity failure (<2.5). Degrees/certificates not recognized by relevant authorities.
Safety standards violation (<2.5). Risk of physical harm, fire, or environmental damage.
Power delivery reliability failure (<2.0). System uptime below minimum viable threshold for productive use.
Fraud prevention failure (<2.0). Inadequate controls against internal or external fraud.
Regulatory non-compliance (<2.5). Violation of core banking/financial regulations (KYC/AML).
Data privacy/sovereignty violation (<2.5). Failure to protect citizen data or adhere to data sovereignty laws.
Corruption/Bribery risk (<2.0). Evidence of corrupt practices or lack of anti-corruption controls.
Patient safety risk (<2.0). Direct risk of harm to patients due to system failure or error.
Clinical accuracy failure (<2.5). Diagnostic or treatment recommendations fall below medical standards.
Network uptime failure (<2.0). Service availability below minimum contractual or regulatory standards.
Power infrastructure dependency failure (<2.0). Critical dependence on unreliable grid without backup.
Passenger safety standards violation (<2.0). Vehicle or operational practices pose direct safety risks.
Insurance/Licensing compliance failure (<2.5). Lack of required operating licenses or insurance coverage.
